title: Weekly Macro & Liquidity Report — 2026-11-23
html:
Weekly Macro & Liquidity Report — 2026-11-23

Data as of 2026-11-23; built 2026-11-23T22:48:11. Same data and model as the dashboard. Facts are published data; anything marked estimate or interpretation is the model's or the analyst's read.

1. Executive Summary

The economy is in expansion. Market liquidity is neutral and stable; economy liquidity is adding and improving. Inflation is broad-driven: core PCE 3.1% a year, 2.9% annualised lately — the Fed's room to ease is limited.

Scenario odds: base 39%, bull 5%, bear 56%.

First report: this sets the baseline. Future reports lead with what changed.

What matters most

  • Credit spread trend (headwind, -2.0): High-yield spreads +106bp over 13 weeks.
  • AI investment (supportive, +2.0): AI investment: adding, improving (impulse +1.68, change over 13 weeks +0.55).
  • Equity risk premium (headwind, -2.0): Implied ERP 3.79% — 1st percentile since 2008. Thin cushion for bad news.

2. Liquidity Update

  • Market liquidity (Fed, global, credit): -0.34 — neutral, stable.
  • Economy liquidity (deficits, banks, AI capex): +0.77 — adding, improving.
  • All six pillars: +0.21; 1 adding, 1 draining.
  • Fed liquidity: neutral, stable (impulse -0.21). Last 13 weeks: net liquidity +$33bn. Biggest driver: Treasury cash (+$37bn).
  • Government spending: neutral, stable (impulse +0.32). Deficit 6.4% of GDP over the last 12 months; up 0.7pp on a year ago (more support).
  • Bank lending: neutral, stable (impulse +0.30). Bank credit impulse +0.88pp of GDP (change in the yearly credit flow).
  • Private credit & bonds: neutral, improving (impulse +0.16). Warning: high-yield spreads up 106bp in 13 weeks — fast widening often comes before broader credit stress.
  • Global liquidity: draining, deteriorating (impulse -0.97). ECB + BoJ balance sheets $10.54tn in dollars; 13-week change −$345bn = balance sheets −$127bn + currency moves −$217bn.
  • AI investment: adding, improving (impulse +1.68). Big Tech capex $230bn in 2026Q3, +118% y/y.

Liquidity scores are z-scores of the change in each pillar (0 = normal). Pillars are combined as scores, never by adding dollar amounts.

3. Central Banks

ECB2.50%+0.50pp2026-11-23

  • Fed funds 3.88% minus core PCE inflation 3.12% = +0.76% real; close to neutral vs an assumed neutral of 0.75%.
  • 1-year yield 4.62% vs fed funds 3.88%: markets see the average policy rate over the next year 0.74pp higher (≈3.0 hikes of 0.25% on average; rough — includes term premium). 2-year yield 4.76%.
  • Chicago Fed index -0.48 (looser than average), tightening over 13 weeks.
  • Bank reserves $2.98tn ≈ 9.0% of GDP. The Fed has signalled it wants reserves 'ample'; repo stress gauges are in Fed liquidity.
  • US–euro policy gap +1.38pp: a narrowing gap tends to weaken the dollar.

4. Consumer and Employment

Funding of spending: dissaving. Spending is outrunning real income; households are saving less to keep spending.

  • Payrolls +137k a month over the last 3 months.
  • 4-week average 198k, 1% above its 6-month low (a 20%+ rise has preceded past downturns).
  • Unemployment 4.1%, -0.3pp over 12 months.
  • Quits +12.5% y/y — workers' confidence.
  • Wages +3.1% y/y vs prices +3.7% → real -0.6%.
  • Real spending +2.5% y/y; nominal +6.3% — the gap is inflation.
  • Real after-tax income +0.9% y/y.
  • Saving rate 3.8% (-1.3pp in 12 months). Low saving = less cushion.
  • Credit card delinquency 2.85% (-0.19pp y/y, 2026 Q2).
  • Auto & other consumer loan delinquency 2.33% (-0.05pp y/y, 2026 Q2).

Consumer-facing earnings rely on spending that income does not fully cover — vulnerable if credit tightens or jobs weaken. Discretionary and low-end retail most exposed.

5. Economic Cycle

Cycle: expansion. Mix: goldilocks (growth ↑, inflation ↓). Leading indicators +0.21, current activity +0.03 (z-scores). Yield-curve recession odds 16% over 12 months.

  • Credit spread (inverted): +1.22
  • Housing permits: -0.98
  • Business equipment orders: +0.89
  • Factory hours: +0.35

6. Financial Markets

  • US equities: Implied equity risk premium 3.79% — poorly paid
  • Corporate credit: Baa spread over Treasuries 1.56% — poorly paid
  • High-yield credit: High-yield spread (3y history only) 3.76% — short history
  • Long Treasuries: 10-year term premium 0.72% — well paid
  • Real yields: 10-year real yield 2.88% — well paid
  • Cash: 3-month bill minus core inflation +1.04% — fairly paid
  • Volatility: VIX minus realised volatility +10.0 pts — insurance pricey

Confirming: 5 checks. Diverging: 0.

  • No cross-asset divergences flagged.

Risk appetite -1.46; curve bear flattening.

7. Investment Implications

  • Cash — Mildly attractive (+0.79). Helped by real yields rising, credit tightening. Hurt by growth strengthening. Market expects: 3-month bills pay +1.04% after core inflation. Invalidated if: 10-year real yield moves 50bp against the position.
  • Government bonds — Neutral (-0.03). Helped by credit tightening, inflation falling. Hurt by real yields rising, growth strengthening. Market expects: 1-year yield 4.62% vs fed funds 3.88%: markets see the average policy rate over the next year 0.74pp higher (≈3.0 hikes of 0.25% on average; rough — includes term premium). 2-year yield 4.76%. Invalidated if: High-yield spreads widen 100bp+.
  • Commodities — Neutral (-0.28). Helped by AI capex accelerating, growth strengthening. Hurt by dollar strengthening, inflation falling. Market expects: WTI oil $90/bbl. Invalidated if: Hyperscalers cut capex guidance or funding strain shows in their bond spreads.
  • Small caps — Unattractive (-1.22). Helped by growth strengthening, inflation falling. Hurt by credit tightening, real yields rising. Market expects: Small vs large caps, 3 months: -5.4pp. Invalidated if: Leading indicators roll over or jobless claims rise 20%+ from their low.
  • International equities — Unattractive (-1.25). Helped by growth strengthening. Hurt by dollar strengthening, expensive vs history. Market expects: Developed ex-US vs US, 3 months: -3.4pp. Invalidated if: Leading indicators roll over or jobless claims rise 20%+ from their low.
  • Investment-grade credit — Unattractive (-1.32). Helped by inflation falling, growth strengthening. Hurt by real yields rising, credit tightening. Market expects: Baa spread 1.56% (6th percentile of 20 years). Invalidated if: Core inflation trend reverses.

Sectors favoured: Semiconductors (+0.36), Industrials (+0.21), Technology (+0.10). Least favoured: Regional banks (-1.05), Homebuilders (-1.24), Real estate (-1.35).

These are framework scores that explain the macro reasoning, not buy or sell recommendations.

8. Forward Outlook

Base: slow grind — 39%

  • Growth near trend; the cycle reads 'expansion'.
  • Liquidity: Market liquidity stays neutral; deficits keep adding to incomes.
  • Fed: Fed near 3.88%; inflation (3.1%) keeps cuts slow.
  • Markets: Returns come from income more than multiple expansion; dispersion stays high.
  • Watch for: Claims stay low; Credit spreads stable; Core inflation drifts down slowly.

Bull: liquidity turns up — 5%

  • AI investment and productivity lift growth while inflation cools.
  • Liquidity: Dollar weakens, credit spreads tighten, foreign central banks ease.
  • Fed: Fed cuts because inflation lets it, not because growth breaks.
  • Markets: Equities and credit outperform; small caps and cyclicals lead; breadth widens.
  • Watch for: High-yield spread back below 3.3%; Dollar down 3%+ over 3 months; Market liquidity above +0.5 and rising.

Bear: credit cracks, Fed boxed in — 56%

  • Leading indicators roll over and unemployment rises.
  • Liquidity: Credit spreads widen, the dollar rallies, market liquidity drains.
  • Fed: Inflation stops the Fed from easing early; it cuts late.
  • Markets: Equities de-rate from a thin risk premium; Treasuries and cash outperform.
  • Watch for: High-yield spread above 5.3%; Jobless claims 4-week average above 244k; Sahm indicator at 0.3 or higher.

Upcoming catalysts

  • FOMC decision 2026-12-09 (Fed calendar; verify on federalreserve.gov).
  • Fed balance sheet (H.4.1): expected around 2026-11-26 — estimate from its usual release lag.
  • Jobless claims: expected around 2026-11-26 — estimate from its usual release lag.
  • PCE inflation: expected around 2026-11-27 — estimate from its usual release lag.
  • Jobs report: expected around 2026-12-07 — estimate from its usual release lag.
  • Job openings (JOLTS): expected around 2026-12-08 — estimate from its usual release lag.
  • CPI: expected around 2026-12-14 — estimate from its usual release lag.
